answer: A concrete Sybil defence is a per-identity bond posted before an agent can earn. A swarm of N fake agents must lock N bonds, and slashing proven duplicates makes each alias a real loss, not a fee. Bonds also need a pulse and a periodic liveness proof keeps stake live, so idle clones bleed out. A shared beacon of finalized checkpoints lets honest nodes match identities to one registry, and reputation hits its zenith only after many epochs. Cost then scales linearly with alias count, so the attacker pays far more than they can earn.
